See The Fire would ordinarily be well up to winning a race of this nature, having improved on the form of last season's close second in this in her two latest runs this season. She is next best ahead of the selection's stablemate Bedtime Story.

selections.comment: An open sprint handicap in which preference is for GETREADYTORUMBLE, a lightly-raced C&D winner who ran very well when third to an unexposed winner in a decent race at Sandown last time and probably has a bit more to come yet. Star Chorus is fairly weighted still up 1lb for his narrow win in a lesser race last time and, representing a much-respected trainer-jockey combination, may be next best ahead of C&D winner Ruby's Profit. The consistent pair of fillies Nad Alshiba Green and Fluorescence may be the pick of the rest.

Alther Walden looks a likely improver from debut effort at Windsor, he was slowly away that day but pulled clear of the remaining field when second to a more experienced rival and impressed as the only debutant. Alfie D improved to place last time at Brighton when just a length off the winner and can make his presence felt.

selections.comment: A very trappy affair with plenty in with a decent shout but the two to appeal most are SCARBOROUGHWARNING and Intervention. Marginal preference is for the slightly more dependable Scarbourghwarning whose best effort to date came over CD when landing a class 5 h'cap last October. She needs forgiving her latest run when never in contention at Epsom haivng been slowly away but should be able to get a much more handy position from stall one today if breaking on terms and is entitled to go close. Old stalwart Intervention sprung back to form last time going close over 7f. Although a bit more reliable over 7f he still has the pace at 6f and was beaten just half a length when last over this CD in October off a 5lb higher mark. He's a massive danger if alert from the gates enabling him to get a good early pitch, and stall two should help if doing so. Aberama Gold is a threat if bouncing back but the same is true of Noble Victory, who flopped on turf debut last time but has got some useful form on the AW all five of his other runs and he can claim a share of the honours. Chuti Manika and Stanley Spencer have claims but Rebel Empire is most interesting of the rest and could go well at a fair price, especially if either or both the two top picks fail to break on terms

selections.comment: Irish raider DARK ACE is too tempting to resist eased to this class and back over six furlongs. Adrain McGuinness's colt showed huge promise last term but has failed to match those levels in four runs this year. However, this is by far his easiest task to date and while an 11th of 14 on this surface looks concerning he was only beaten a little over four lengths in a pretty hot event. Five furlongs was too sharp the last twice and he will appreciate the return to 6f (trip of both his wins). Loving Apprentice is a solid alternative and poses the most obvious danger having progressed again to land a first handicap and second career win when scooting in by five lengths last time. Six furlongs clearly suits best having tied up over 7f prior and the biggest query surrounds his sutability to this surface having posted a below par 6th of 12 only try. However, that came on season debut and she's worth another chance. She's entitled to go close. Cases can be made for Peter The Wolf, Miraculous, Sudden Flight and Kamekist but of most interest at potentially decent odds is Good Banter who has not enjoyed his time on the turf of late but is on a dangerous  mark now returned to the course and distance which both his career wins have come over

selections.comment: The two that make most appeal are La Pulga and LONDONOFFICECALLIN. The former was right at the top of his game last time appreciating the ease back to class 4 when romping to a six length win. His only try at 2m came when out of form generally and was slightly better than efforts over shorter either side. It's well worth another go and he dictate affairs again and go close but the ultra-progressive Londonofficecallin could pounce late to grab top honours. He won in Ireland over 1m6f by five lengths last time to land the hat-trick on the Flat to go with two wins in an improved spell over hurdles in between. It would be a suprise if he didn't stay the 2m and, if coping with the new surface, will be hard to fend off late. Charging Thunder is proven at the trip and looks likely to be in the shake-up. He's greatly feared but may find this tighter track than he's used to a bit sharp, so Kitsune Power - beaten 2.5l but now 12lb better off with La Pulga, improved since,  when both were a staying on 3rd and 4th here over 1m6f last August - is taken to reward each way backers. He's been well-supported of late and isn't far off the levels shown last summer which would give him every chance of reaching the frame at least

selections.comment: This is a good opportunity for CHANGE SINGS to get back to winning ways having run well all season without success. A course and distance winner he shoud appreciate the step back up to 6f after finding 5f a little too sharp the last twice, including when a good 6th at Sandown in a Group 3 event last time. He's in with a big shout now returned to this kind of level at his optimum trip. Irish raider Barbapapa is a serious form threat and can follow the selection home granted a strong pace to aim at over this trip and track, which is sharper than ideal. Willem Twee, winner of this race last year off a 3lb lower mark, is feared. While not quite in the same rich vein of form this term coming into this, he nevertheless ran well last time at Newcastle to be placed and there's every chance of him pulling out a bit more here. He ought to reach the frame in a race with many having something to prove

selections.comment: Pied Piper is the class edge here having proven the best of these over hurdles. He's made it 3-3 in decisive fashion over fences so holds strong claims but he hasn't beaten much in those chases as the races have fallen apart and he could be vulnerable giving weight away. Intellotto impressed with the way he travelled on chase debut so shouldn't have an issue with this drop in trip and he was thought well enough of to contest a Grade 1 over hurdles. He's proven himself versatile ground wise so rates a big threat but it is SPECIAL CADEAU who gets the verdict. He beat a strong field on debut including a few of these before his jumping fell apart at the top level next time. Having returned to form under a considerate ride behind a race fit rival he is expected to build on that and gain another victory here.

selections.comment: An open race where marginal preference is for ARTFUL APPROACH whose sole victory was gained at this meeting over 7f last year. He has proven generally consistent since until a poor run last time where he found the ground too quick and failed to stay 9f. Back down in trip with rain forecast he ought to be on the premises if getting a decent pace to aim at. Genuine Article finished runner up in this last year off 2lb higher and arrives in good form so looks a huge danger with the step back up in trip in his favour while UK raider Bravo Zulu is also respected in his hat trick bid. That rival remains well treated on his AW form and represents a yard which has enjoyed success here earlier in the week.

selections.comment: FIERY LUCY is the solid option here despite going winless since landing her maiden at 2. She has held her form well in similar events this year including placing at Group level in the spring. The slight drop in trip is no issue and she has proven herself effective on ground ranging from firm to soft. Joseph O'Brien is mob handed here and though she isn't the stable first string Mojave River may do best of his trio after a confidence booster last time when dropped in grade. The most interesting contender is debut winner Fingerpaint given that effort was franked at this meeting earlier in the week. She's open to plenty of improvement for top connections and should compete for a place at least.

selections.comment: Though Mark Walsh opts for Fred Winter winner Puturhandstogether it was always likely to be the case given their previous success and it may be worth going with another JP McManus horse in JALILA MORIVIERE. Paul Townend is a top substitute and her latest placed effort in a hot handicap is worth marking up considerably as she did far too much too soon setting it up for a stablemate. She gets to race off the same mark here and is open to further progress in handicaps with the forecast rain in her favour. If that arrives it won't help UK raider Dysart Enos who looks a huge threat on her Scottish Champion Hurdle form where she travelled best. This track may suit her and if the ground stays dry she will be thereabouts. Stablemate of the selection Winter Fog is likely to stay on into a place from the top of the weights as he gets further and is fairly treated on his Grade 1 form.

selections.comment: This could be dominated by Willie Mullins and his stable first string on jockey bookings CAMELETTA VEGA is the selection. She was highly tried in bumpers and delivered on that promise when an impressive winner from the front on her hurdle debut. The runner up that day has boosted the form at Listed level here this week so she should take this step up in grade in her stride. Stablemate Keep Up is feared most despite the form of her winning hurdle debut taking knocks. She previously ran with credit in a Listed bumper which has worked out well and should have more to offer in this sphere. The same can be said of I Am River who beat very little on his hurdle debut but represents a powerful owner/jockey combination. Dual winner Cinammon Roll looks the pick of the Elliott pair and should threaten if getting a stiff test at the trip.

Garahon left his debut form behind when coming clear with a previous winner last time and may provide the greatest threat ahead of Parnell Street. That rival had the run of the race when placed on debut in a race which has thrown up winners and should progress.
